olivia: quick thread — decision needed: who owns the prefetch window by default across SDKs (python/ts/go)? server-side, sdk-side, or opt-in? i'll list tradeoffs.

mike: +1. currently server and clients both prefetch sometimes, which doubles work.

sara: leaning server-owned default with sdk opt-out. centralized knobs, telemetry, easier global rate limits.

raj: server-owned hides client patterns and hurts private/on-prem installs. client-local defaults are friendlier for private deployments.

olivia: compromise proposal: hosted = server-owned default; Dedicated/Private = client-owned default. keep same SDK surface, only default differs by environment metadata.

casey: suggested API shape (parity across langs):
```
// pseudo config
client = RedwoodClient({
  prefetch: {
    mode: "auto", // auto/server|client|disabled
    window_tokens: 256,
  }
})
```
auto resolves to server when hosting metadata present, else client-local.

mike: two followups: who does backoff/retry when prefetch hits limits? and how do we avoid double-prefetch when mode=auto and an old SDK is used?

sara: 1) backoff belongs to the component doing the prefetch; server-side prefetch uses server rate-limiter. SDKs must implement idempotent cancel+resume. 2) add capability header: `x-prefetch-handled: true` so SDKs detect server handling and disable local prefetch. do a small versioned handshake.

raj: also think about transport: streaming vs unary control. streaming allows server push of prefetch hints; unary uses headers or a small API call. streaming is better for low-latency but heavier to implement.

olivia: interop plan: default to unary headers + optional control stream for long-lived sessions. SDKs open stream via a Session object to receive `prefetch_window_adjust` events.

casey: impl sketch:
```
// python: session = client.open_session(prefetch_stream=True)
// ts: const session = client.session({prefetchStream: true})
```
session listens for `prefetch_window_adjust`.

mike: retries: speculative prefetch can consume tokens that then error; how do we account or roll back?

sara: bill speculative tokens only if used by model. track per-token attribution and mark telemetry `prefetch_speculative=true`. default conservative window (128 tokens) to limit waste.

raj: long-term: unify prefetch + kv-cache into single local cache policy module so strategies can be swapped without changing API. add to roadmap.

olivia: decision for now: hosted server-owned default, sdk opt-out flag, capability header `x-prefetch-handled`, unary header plus optional control stream, conservative default window=128 tokens. add RFC and tests.

casey: i'll open RFC PR with API examples, header names, and backward-compatible handshake plus migration notes.

mike: add e2e test plan simulating old sdk + new server to confirm no double-prefetch.

dev-bot: deploy-bot: created issue INFR-2145: "prefetch ownership defaults + sdk handshake" assigned to @casey.

olivia: tagging followups: @sara spec telemetry labels, @raj draft session stream proto, @mike add e2e tests.

sara: on it.

raj: proto draft incoming, will ping for review.

casey: RFC PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/701 — feedback welcome.

olivia: thanks everyone. closing thread, reopen in sync channel if needed. :rocket:
